correctness.rationale: Every nontrivial graphical EFX comparison arises when a receiving endpoint has a second, irrelevant-to-the-envying-agent edge. The proof translates these comparisons bijectively to internal 0011 sink patterns with two explicit weight inequalities, then gives exact bounds and a unique run decomposition for the maximum. Formal power-series coefficient extraction and a rational simple-pole calculation prove the recurrence and golden-ratio asymptotic. A separate literal EFX verifier agrees on 397,362 finite states; finite enumeration is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural symmetric graphical EFX model on paths has a sharp, exact prevalence interval from linear to golden-ratio exponential. The path sink criterion makes this prevalence computable and shows that arbitrarily small monotone weight changes destroy an exponentially large fraction of fair orientations. This gives a substantive sensitivity boundary rather than a routine existence or normalization check.
